question: A patient complaining of nausea might actually be suffering from which non-gut condition?
explanation: Conditions like heart attacks can present primarily as upper tummy distress because nerve signals from the heart and gut share similar pathways to the brain. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h1)

question: Why is taking a detailed history so important for tummy complaints?

options.A: Doctors are not allowed to touch the patient first
options.B: Patients rarely tell the truth about their pain
options.C: Subjective complaints often start before physical signs show up
options.D: It replaces the need for any laboratory investigations

explanation: Listening closely to how a symptom started helps nurses guide early physical assessment and targeted care. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h1)

question: How do patients typically describe pain coming from internal gut organs?
explanation: Stretching of hollow organs sends generalized signals to the brain, making the exact spot hard for the patient to point out. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h2)

question: What causes fluid to build up in the intestines during osmotic diarrhea?

options.A: Unabsorbed particles drawing water into the gut
options.B: Rapid inflammation of the stomach lining
options.C: Complete blockage of the large intestine
options.D: Bacterial toxins directly stimulating fluid secretion

explanation: Osmotic diarrhea happens when particles stay inside the bowel instead of being absorbed, pulling water along with them. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h2)

question: Pain from an inflamed appendix is most commonly felt in which area?
explanation: The appendix sits near the meeting point of the small and large intestines, which usually maps to the lower right side of the belly. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h3)

question: Why must a nurse listen to bowel sounds with a stethoscope before pressing on the belly?

options.A: Listening is less important than pressing on the belly
options.B: Pressing can alter natural bowel sounds and mislead findings
options.C: Auscultation warms up the stethoscope for the patient
options.D: Patients get scared if you touch them right away

explanation: Pushing on the abdomen can stimulate movement in the intestines, creating false impressions of how fast or slow the bowel is working. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h3)

question: Vomiting that smells like stool is a classic sign of what condition?
explanation: When the lower bowel is blocked, waste backs up through the digestive tract and eventually comes out through the mouth. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h4)

question: A patient with a hard stool blockage passes small amounts of liquid. What is this called?

options.A: Rapid transit syndrome due to high dietary fiber intake
options.B: Pseudo-diarrhea from liquid stool seeping around a hard mass
options.C: Normal recovery phase following severe chronic constipation
options.D: Primary secretory diarrhea caused by a bacterial infection

explanation: Liquid waste finds a way around the blockage in the rectum, creating a false sign of watery diarrhea while the main mass stays stuck. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h4)

question: What is the medical term for dark, tarry stools caused by bleeding in the upper gut?
explanation: Stomach acid and digestive juices break down blood hemoglobin as it moves through the gut, turning the stool dark and sticky. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h5)

question: Why does bleeding from the colon usually show up as bright red blood in the stool?

options.A: Colonic blood mixes with bile salts to turn bright red
options.B: The blood does not get digested or exposed to stomach acid for long
options.C: Lower gut blood contains more oxygen than upper gut blood
options.D: The rectum adds pigment to the blood during defecation

explanation: Since the bleeding happens near the end of the digestive tract, the blood passes out quickly without changing color from stomach acid. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h5)

question: Long-term trouble absorbing nutrients in the small intestine commonly leads to which problem?

options.D: Sudden high fever and skin rashes

explanation: Not being able to take in vitamins and minerals like iron and calcium slowly drains body stores and weakens tissues. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h6)

question: Why does severe protein loss from chronic gut disease cause swelling in the legs?

options.A: Blocked lymphatic vessels in the gut back up fluid into the legs
options.B: The patient drinks too much water to compensate for the diarrhea
options.C: Kidneys shut down completely due to a lack of dietary salt
options.D: Low blood protein reduces pressure inside blood vessels, pushing fluid into tissues

explanation: Blood proteins normally hold fluid inside vessels. When protein levels drop, fluid leaks out into the body tissues. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h6)

question: What is the main nursing priority right after a patient has an upper gut endoscopy?

options.A: Measuring abdominal girth every fifteen minutes
options.B: Administering a strong laxative to clear the bowels
options.C: Encouraging immediate heavy meals to test digestion
options.D: Checking for the return of the patient's gag reflex

explanation: Numbing medicine sprayed in the throat blocks normal swallowing, putting the patient at risk of choking if food or drink is given too soon. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h7)

question: Which complication must a nurse watch for most closely after a colonoscopy?
explanation: Passing instruments through the colon carries a small risk of tearing the intestinal wall, which causes severe pain and a hard belly. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h7)
